findings.reason: naming the existing channel turns §4 from a new subsystem into a documented extension of one, which is the difference between adding surface and deepening it.
findings.text: §4 proposes a new inbox and a new coordinator-side writer without naming the durable per-run channel it duplicates (reckon/crew/dispatch.py `peer_ask`/`peer_read`/`_channel_root`), whose endpoint is already `run_dir(run_id)/peer-channel` and already composed into every worker prompt at reckon/crew/prompts.py:619

findings.reason: the owner to extend is dispatch.py's channel; forking a parallel inbox-into-run-dir path gives two writers of the same run directory that will drift, which is the exact duplicate the rubric names.
findings.text: the plan adds a second durable per-run message writer/reader beside the channel already owned by `peer_ask`/`peer_read`/`_channel_root` in dispatch.py

findings.reason: the honest change is to relax peer_ask's sender/wiring gate or add a coordinator-sender path through it, so the plan should justify a new writer or drop it.
findings.text: the coordinator-side writer is `peer_ask` minus its adjacent-peer wiring requirement (peer_ask already persists a durable message into both run directories), and the plan does not state why peer_ask cannot be extended to admit a coordinator sender

findings.reason: consolidating the inbox onto the existing channel module keeps the new behaviour (a checkpoint read) behind the interface that already exists, rather than adding three shallow points of contact.
findings.text: §4 spreads one capability across three surfaces — a prompt-contract edit in reckon/crew/prompts.py, a new coordinator-side writer in the CLI, and a new directory layout — where the existing channel is a single module hiding the store and the blocking read behind three functions

findings.reason: the section must account for the added interface surface in its own text, either by extending the existing `peer-*` client rather than adding an option, or by stating why nothing can be.
findings.text: the section adds a coordinator-side writer, which is a new CLI option on a surface already at cli_options 317, and names nothing it retires or merges

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the transport already hides the store and the blocking read behind peer_ask/peer_read; §4 splits the same functionality across a prompt-contract edit, a new coordinator-side writer and a new directory instead of one module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements the per-run durable channel owned by reckon/crew/dispatch.py rather than extending it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4/§7 add a coordinator-side writer (a CLI option) and the section names nothing it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §4 adds an "inbox" subsystem and, in its own text, cites no existing mechanism, though the durable per-run channel it most resembles already exists at reckon/crew/dispatch.py and is already in the worker prompt at reckon/crew/prompts.py:619.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the coordinator-side writer §7 names is peer_ask with its wiring requirement removed, and the plan nowhere says why peer_ask cannot be extended instead.
